Theorem
[structure of compact manifolds with nonnegative Ricci curvature]

Source: petersen:page-0319, petersen:page-0320 ↗ thm:pet-ch7-splitting-theorem ↗ lem:pet-ch7-ray-line-existence 1. ch7:7.3.11Suppose $(M,g)$ is compact with $\Ric \ge 0$. Then:

  1. the universal cover $(\tilde M,\tilde g)$ splits isometrically as $N\times \mathbb {R}^k$, with $N$ compact and containing no lines;

  2. $\Iso (\tilde M)=\Iso (N)\times \Iso (\mathbb {R}^k)$;

  3. there is a finite normal subgroup $G\subset \pi _1(M)$ with $\pi _1(M)/G\cong \pi _1(M)\cap \Iso (\mathbb {R}^k)$, and a finite-index subgroup $\mathbb {Z}^k\subset \pi _1(M)\cap \Iso (\mathbb {R}^k)$.

Proof

↗ thm:pet-ch7-structure-theorem \sketch Iterate the splitting theorem on the universal cover to obtain $N\times \mathbb R^k$ with $N$ line-free; compactness of $N$ follows by recentering a ray under the cocompact deck action, which would otherwise produce a line. Isometries preserve the Euclidean line factors, so the isometry group splits. The kernel of the Euclidean projection is finite, and the translation subgroup is a discrete cocompact lattice, hence a finite-index $\mathbb Z^k$.

□
